provenance.what: PaddleX's textline orientation (PP-LCNet_x1_0_textline_ori) as frozen PaddleOCR runs it, on the synthetic scene and on frozen Python's working image of each of the 13 stored bay photos, and its half turn
provenance.recorded_by: M29 P6, a scratch script: preprocess.py's load_image, warp_to_rect (by det_boxes.json's quad), _resize and enhance, then the live OCR pipeline (PaddleOCR as paddle.py constructs it, oneDNN off): its _crop_by_polys on det_boxes.json's sorted boxes (each crop checked against rec_texts.json's digest), and its textline_orientation_model's own preprocessors (ReadImage format RGB, Resize to 160x80 with cv2.INTER_LINEAR, Normalize, ToCHW, ToBatch), runner and Topk, in batches of 6 in box order; the predictor's own call gave the same classes. The half turn is the pipeline's rotate_image(crop, 180)
provenance.scene: rectify/scene.png: batches are the textline input tensors of rec_reference.json's 60 crops (cropped by PaddleX) and a 61st, the scene's own pixels at exact (already 160x80, so Resize leaves it), in batches of 6, each with its shape and SHA-256 (f32 little-endian, NCHW); turned is rotate_image(crop, 180) on each of the 60, its size and the SHA-256 of its pixels as RGB
provenance.photos: per photo: classes, per crop in reading order, Topk's class and the model's two probabilities (0_degree, 180_degree); batches, each batch's members, shape and input-tensor SHA-256; flipped and flipped_batches, the same for every crop turned upside down by a true flip (crop[::-1, ::-1]), because the pipeline classified no crop of the 13 as upside down
provenance.no_crop_turns: on all 13, frozen PaddleOCRRecognizer.recognize's own textline_orientation_angles were all 0, and its boxes were spec/vectors/screen/corpus/'s exactly
